subject: chem
title: Chemical Thermodynamics
syllabus: Fundamentals of thermodynamics: System and surroundings, extensive and intensive properties, state functions, Entropy, types of processes. The first law of thermodynamics — Concept of work, heat internal energy and enthalpy, heat capacity, molar heat capacity; Hess's law of constant heat summation; Enthalpies of bond dissociation, combustion, formation, atomization, sublimation, phase transition, hydration, ionization and solution. The second law of thermodynamics — Spontaneity of processes; ΔS of the universe and ΔG of the system as criteria for spontaneity. ΔG° (Standard Gibbs energy change) and equilibrium constant.

topics.law: First law, work, heat & ΔH vs ΔU

cards.t: System, state and the first law
body: Open / closed / isolated systems. State functions (U, H, S, G, p, V, T) depend only on the state; q and w depend on the path.
Extensive (mass, volume, U, H, G) scale with amount; intensive (T, p, density, concentration, molar quantities) do not.
ΔU = q + w (w = work done ON the system; chemistry sign convention)
Isolated, adiabatic: q = 0. Free expansion into vacuum: w = 0 (and for an ideal gas ΔT = 0).

check.why: Same for a cup or a bucket.

body: Irreversible: w = −p_{ext}ΔV. Reversible isothermal: w = −nRT ln\f{V_{2}}{V_{1}} = −2.303nRT log\f{p_{1}}{p_{2}}
Isothermal ideal gas: ΔU = 0 so q = −w. Adiabatic: q = 0 so ΔU = w = nC_{V}ΔT.
Reversible expansion gives the MOST work out; reversible compression needs the LEAST work in; more stages → closer to reversible.
Units: 1 L atm = 101.3 J.
ΔH = ΔU + Δn_{g}RT
Bomb calorimeter (constant V) measures ΔU; coffee-cup (constant p) measures ΔH. Heat = C × ΔT.
Count only GAS moles for Δn_{g} (water as liquid counts 0).
Phase changes: Δ_{fus}H, Δ_{vap}H, Δ_{sub}H = Δ_{fus}H + Δ_{vap}H. Heating a phase: q = nC_{p}ΔT.

check.q: C(s) + O₂ → CO₂: ΔH vs ΔU

body: ΔH depends only on start and end — add equations, add their ΔH. Reverse → change sign; multiply → multiply ΔH.
Δ_{r}H° = ΣνΔ_{f}H°(products) − ΣνΔ_{f}H°(reactants)
Elements in their standard state have Δ_{f}H° = 0. From combustion data: Δ_{f}H = Σ(Δ_{f}H of CO_{2}, H_{2}O) − Δ_{c}H.
Heat of solution = lattice (to break) + hydration; heat of neutralisation (strong acid + strong base) ≈ −57 kJ mol^{−1}.
ΔH = Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed) (all gases)
Average bond enthalpy = atomisation enthalpy ÷ number of bonds (e.g. C−H = \f{1}{4}Δ_{a}H(CH_{4})).
Δ_{f}H = Δ_{sub}H + IE + ½D + EG − U_{lattice}
Energy per bond = \f{ΔH (J/mol)}{N_{A}} = \f{hc}{λ}.
Entropy measures spreading of energy/disorder: gas ≫ liquid > solid. ΔS_{univ} > 0 for any spontaneous change.
ΔS = \f{q_{rev}}{T}, ΔS_{trans} = \f{ΔH_{trans}}{T}, ΔS = nC_{p} ln\f{T_{2}}{T_{1}}
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; ΔG < 0 spontaneous, = 0 equilibrium; ΔG° = −RT ln K
(+,+) high T only; (−,−) low T only; (−,+) always; (+,−) never. Crossover at T = \f{ΔH}{ΔS}.

formulas: Δ_{f}H = S + IE + ½D + EG − U
traps: w is work done ON the system: expansion gives w < 0.
Δn_g counts only gases — liquid water does not count.
ΔS is in J, ΔH in kJ — convert before ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.
Elements have zero Δ_fH° but NOT zero entropy.
Bond-enthalpy method works only for gases.
Heat released means ΔH is negative: "+ x kcal" written on the product side is ΔH = −x.

steps.note: q, w, ΔU, ΔH and calorimetry
Entropy, Gibbs energy, the four sign cases

pyq.q: Choose the correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition from the following :
sol: Adiabatic → q = 0. Free expansion (into vacuum, p_{ext} = 0) → w = 0.
So ΔU = 0, and for an ideal gas U depends only on T → ΔT = 0.

pyq.q: Arrange the following in order of magnitude of work done by the system/on the system at constant temperature. (a) |w_{reversible}| for expansion in infinite stages. (b) |w_{irreversible}| for expansion in single stage. (c) |w_{reversible}| for compression in infinite stages. (d) |w_{irreversible}| for compression in single stage. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Take 1 → 2 volume at RT = 1: reversible either way |w| = ln 2 ≈ 0.69 (a = c).
Single-stage expansion against the final pressure ½: |w| = 0.5 (b). Single-stage compression against pressure 2: |w| = 1 (d).

pyq.q: Which of the following properties will change when system containing solution 1 (10 mol of solute x + 10 L of water) will become solution 2 (1 L of solution 1 + 1 mol of solute x + 1 L of water)?
sol: Solution 2 = 1 mol x in 1 L + 1 mol x in 1 L — the same 1 mol per litre composition, so intensive properties (concentration, density, molar heat capacity) stay the same.
The amount is different (2 L instead of 10 L), so an EXTENSIVE property like G changes.

pyq.q: A sample of n-octane (1.14 g) was completely burnt in excess of oxygen in a bomb calorimeter, whose heat capacity is 5 kJ K^{−1}. As a result of combustion reaction, the temperature of the calorimeter is increased by 5 K. The magnitude of the heat of combustion of octane at constant volume is ____ kJ mol^{−1} (nearest integer).
sol: ΔU_{c} = 2500 kJ mol^{−1} (bomb calorimeter = constant volume).

pyq.q: One mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly from 10 dm^{3} to 20 dm^{3} at 300 K. ΔU, q and work done in the process respectively are (Given: R = 8.3 J K^{−1} mol^{−1}, ln 10 = 2.3, log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48)
Consider the given data : (a) HCl(g) + 10H_{2}O(l) → HCl.10H_{2}O, ΔH = −69.01 kJ mol^{−1} (b) HCl(g) + 40H_{2}O(l) → HCl.40H_{2}O, ΔH = −72.79 kJ mol^{−1}. Choose the correct statement :
sol: (a) and (b) differ only in the amount of water, and their ΔH differ → (1) ✓.
Dilution: −72.79 − (−69.01) = −3.78 kJ (heat RELEASED, not +3.78). Both are exothermic.
o: The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent.
The heat of dilution for the HCl (HCl.10H_{2}O to HCl.40H_{2}O) is 3.78 kJ mol^{−1}.
Dissolution of gas in water is an endothermic process.
The heat of formation of HCl solution is represented by both (a) and (b).

pyq.q: Three moles of an ideal gas are compressed isothermally from 60 L to 20 L using constant pressure of 5 atm. The magnitude of heat exchange Q for the compression is ____ Lit. atm.
sol: w = −p_{ext}ΔV = −5(20 − 60) = +200 L atm (work done ON the gas).
Isothermal ideal gas: ΔU = 0 → Q = −w = −200 L atm (heat released); magnitude 200.

pyq.q: The heat of combustion of solid benzoic acid at constant volume is −321.30 kJ at 27 °C. The heat of combustion at constant pressure is (−321.30 − xR) kJ, the value of x is

An ideal gas, C̄_{V} = \f{5}{2}R, is expanded adiabatically against a constant pressure of 1 atm untill it doubles in volume. If the initial temperature and pressure is 298 K and 5 atm, respectively then the final temperature is ____ K (nearest integer).
Total enthalpy change for freezing of 1 mol of water at 10 °C to ice at −10 °C is (Given: Δ_{fus}H = x kJ/mol, C_{p}[H_{2}O(l)] = y J mol^{−1} K^{−1}, C_{p}[H_{2}O(s)] = z J mol^{−1} K^{−1})
sol: Cool water 10 → 0 °C: −10y J; freeze: −x kJ = −1000x J; cool ice 0 → −10 °C: −10z J.

pyq.q: Standard enthalpy of vapourisation for CCl_{4} is 30.5 kJ mol^{−1}. Heat required for vapourisation of 284 g of CCl_{4} at constant temperature is ____ kJ. (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1}; C = 12, Cl = 35.5)

Given below are two statements: Statement I : For an ideal gas, heat capacity at constant volume is always greater than the heat capacity at constant pressure. Statement II : In a constant volume process, no work is produced and all the heat withdrawn goes into the chaotic motion and is reflected by a temperature increase of the ideal gas. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: C_{p} − C_{V} = R > 0: at constant pressure part of the heat is spent as expansion work → I false.
At constant volume w = 0, so q = ΔU, raising T → II true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: If 5 moles of an ideal gas expands from 10 L to a volume of 100 L at 300 K under isothermal and reversible condition then work, w, is −x J. The value of x is ____ . (Given R = 8.314 J K^{−1} mol^{−1})

Arrange the following isothermal processes in order of the magnitude of the work (p−V) involved between states 1 and 2. A. Expansion in single stage w_{A} B. Expansion in multi stages w_{B} C. Compression in single stage w_{C} D. Compression in multi stages w_{D}. Choose the correct option.
sol: Expansion (1 → 2 V): the more stages, the closer to reversible → MORE work out: |w_{B}| > |w_{A}|.
Compression: the more stages, the LESS work needed: |w_{C}| > |w_{D}|; and any compression needs more than the matching expansion gives.

pyq.q: Match List-I with List-II. Given V_{1} and V_{2} are initial and final volumes respectively. List-I (Isothermal process): A. Reversible expansion B. Free expansion C. Irreversible Compression D. Cyclic reversible. List-II (Expression): I. q = 0 II. q = nRT ln\f{V_{2}}{V_{1}} III. w = −p_{ext}(V_{1} − V_{2}) IV. \f{q_{rev}}{T} = 0. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Reversible isothermal expansion: q = −w = nRT ln\f{V_{2}}{V_{1}} (II). Free expansion: w = 0, ΔU = 0 → q = 0 (I).

Irreversible compression: w = −p_{ext}(V_{2} − V_{1}) = p_{ext}(V_{1} − V_{2}); List-II writes it the other way round — still the one irreversible-work entry (III). Cyclic reversible: ΔS = Σ\f{q_{rev}}{T} = 0 (IV).

pyq.q: 20.0 dm^{3} of an ideal gas 'X' at 600 K and 0.5 MPa undergoes isothermal reversible expansion until pressure of the gas is 0.2 MPa. Which of the following option is correct? (Given: log 2 = 0.3010 and log 5 = 0.6989)
sol: Isothermal ideal gas: ΔU = ΔH = 0, q = −w ≈ +9.1 kJ.

pyq.q: Combustion of 1 mole of benzene is expressed as C_{6}H_{6}(l) + \f{15}{2}O_{2}(g) → 6CO_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}O(l). The standard enthalpy of combustion of 2 mol of benzene is −'x' kJ. x = ____. (1) Standard enthalpy of formation of 1 mol of C_{6}H_{6}(l), for the reaction 6C(graphite) + 3H_{2}(g) → C_{6}H_{6}(l) is 48.5 kJ mol^{−1}. (2) Standard enthalpy of formation of 1 mol of CO_{2}(g) is −393.5 kJ mol^{−1}. (3) Standard enthalpy of formation of 1 mol of H_{2}O(l) is −286 kJ mol^{−1}.
The hydration energies of K^{+} and Cl^{−} are −x and −y kJ/mol respectively. If lattice energy of KCl is −z kJ/mol, then the heat of solution of KCl is :
sol: Dissolving = break the lattice (+z, the reverse of forming it) + hydrate the ions (−x − y).

pyq.q: The heat of solution of anhydrous CuSO_{4} and CuSO_{4}·5H_{2}O are −70 kJ mol^{−1} and +12 kJ mol^{−1} respectively. The heat of hydration of CuSO_{4} to CuSO_{4}·5H_{2}O is −x kJ. The value of x is ____.
sol: CuSO_{4} → solution (−70) = CuSO_{4} → CuSO_{4}·5H_{2}O (ΔH_{hyd}) + CuSO_{4}·5H_{2}O → solution (+12).

pyq.q: Consider the following data. (i) 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → Al_{2}Cl_{6}(aq) + 3H_{2}(g) + 1200 kJ/mol (ii) H_{2}(g) + Cl_{2}(g) → 2HCl(g) + 164 kJ/mol (iii) HCl(g) + aq → HCl(aq) + 83 kJ/mol (iv) Al_{2}Cl_{6}(s) + aq → Al_{2}Cl_{6}(aq) + 663 kJ/mol. The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid Al_{2}Cl_{6} is :

Consider the following cases of standard enthalpy of reaction (ΔH°_{r} in kJ mol^{−1}): C_{2}H_{6}(g) + \f{7}{2}O_{2}(g) → 2CO_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}O(l), ΔH°_{1} = −1550; C(graphite) + O_{2}(g) → CO_{2}(g), ΔH°_{2} = −393.5; H_{2}(g) + \f{1}{2}O_{2}(g) → H_{2}O(l), ΔH°_{3} = −286. The magnitude of ΔH°_{f}(C_{2}H_{6}, g) is ____ kJ mol^{−1} (Nearest integer).
S(g) + \f{3}{2}O_{2}(g) → SO_{3}(g) + 2x kcal; SO_{2}(g) + \f{1}{2}O_{2}(g) → SO_{3}(g) + y kcal. The heat of formation of SO_{2}(g) is given by :
sol: "+ heat" on the right means ΔH is negative: ΔH_{1} = −2x, ΔH_{2} = −y.

pyq.q: Consider the following data : Heat of formation of CO_{2}(g) = −393.5 kJ mol^{−1}, Heat of formation of H_{2}O(l) = −286.0 kJ mol^{−1}, Heat of combustion of benzene = −3267.0 kJ mol^{−1}. The heat of formation of benzene is ____ kJ mol^{−1}. (Nearest integer)

Two reactions are given below: 2Fe(s) + \f{3}{2}O_{2}(g) → Fe_{2}O_{3}(s), ΔH° = −822 kJ/mol; C(s) + \f{1}{2}O_{2}(g) → CO(g), ΔH° = −110 kJ/mol. Then enthalpy change for following reaction 3C(s) + Fe_{2}O_{3}(s) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO(g) is ____.

If 3.365 g of ethanol (l) is burnt completely in a bomb calorimeter at 298.15 K, the heat produced is 99.472 kJ. The |ΔH°_{f}| of ethanol at 298.15 K is ____ × 10^{2} kJ mol^{−1}. (Nearest integer) Given: Standard enthalpy for combustion of graphite = −393.5 kJ mol^{−1}; Standard enthalpy of formation of water (l) = −285.8 kJ mol^{−1}; Molar mass in g mol^{−1} of C, H, O are 12, 1 and 16 respectively

Consider the reaction 2H_{2}S(g) + 3O_{2}(g) → 2H_{2}O(l) + 2SO_{2}(g). The magnitude of enthalpy change for the reaction in kJ mol^{−1} is ____. (Nearest integer) Given: Δ_{f}H°(H_{2}S) = −20.1 kJ mol^{−1}, Δ_{f}H°(H_{2}O) = −286.0 kJ mol^{−1}, Δ_{f}H°(SO_{2}) = −297.0 kJ mol^{−1}

The magnitude of enthalpy of formation of ethane (C_{2}H_{6}) from ethylene by addition of hydrogen where the bond energies of C−H, C−C, C=C, H−H are 414 kJ, 347 kJ, 615 kJ and 435 kJ respectively is ____ kJ.

Consider the following data: Δ_{f}H°(methane, g) = −X kJ mol^{−1}; Enthalpy of sublimation of graphite = Y kJ mol^{−1}; Dissociation enthalpy of H_{2} = Z kJ mol^{−1}. The bond enthalpy of C−H bond is given by :

The bond dissociation enthalpy of X_{2} ΔH°_{bond} calculated from the given data is ____ kJ mol^{−1}. (Nearest integer) M^{+}X^{−}(s) → M^{+}(g) + X^{−}(g), ΔH°_{lattice} = 800 kJ mol^{−1}; M(s) → M(g), ΔH°_{sub} = 100 kJ mol^{−1}; M(g) → M^{+}(g) + e^{−}(g), ΔH°_{i} = 500 kJ mol^{−1}; X(g) + e^{−}(g) → X^{−}(g), ΔH°_{eg} = −300 kJ mol^{−1}; M(s) + \f{1}{2}X_{2}(g) → M^{+}X^{−}(s), ΔH°_{f} = −400 kJ mol^{−1} [Given : M^{+}X^{−} is a pure ionic compound and X forms a diatomic molecule X_{2} in gaseous state]
sol: Born–Haber: ΔH_{f} = sub + IE + ½D + EG − lattice.

pyq.q: The formation enthalpies, ΔH°_{f} for H(g) and O(g) are 220.0 and 250.0 kJ mol^{−1}, respectively, at 298.15 K, and ΔH°_{f} for H_{2}O(g) is −242.0 kJ mol^{−1} at the same temperature. The average bond enthalpy of the O−H bond in water at 298.15 K is ____ kJ mol^{−1} (nearest integer).

If the enthalpy of sublimation of Li is 155 kJ mol^{−1}, enthalpy of dissociation of F_{2} is 150 kJ mol^{−1}, ionization enthalpy of Li is 520 kJ mol^{−1}, electron gain enthalpy of F is −313 kJ mol^{−1}, standard enthalpy of formation of LiF is −594 kJ mol^{−1}. The magnitude of lattice enthalpy of LiF is ____ kJ mol^{−1}. (Nearest Integer)
sol: Lattice (LiF → ions) = sub + ½D + IE + EG − ΔH_{f}.

pyq.q: The heat of atomisation of methane and ethane are 'x' kJ mol^{−1} and 'y' kJ mol^{−1} respectively. The longest wavelength (λ) of light capable of breaking the C−C bond can be expressed in SI unit as:
sol: C−H = \f{x}{4}; ethane: C−C + 6\f{x}{4} = y → C−C = y − \f{3x}{2} kJ mol^{−1}.

pyq.q: Let us consider a reversible reaction at temperature, T. In this reaction, both ΔH and ΔS were observed to have positive values. If the equilibrium temperature is Te, then the reaction becomes spontaneous at:
sol: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = 0 at Te = \f{ΔH}{ΔS}; with both positive, ΔG < 0 when T > Te.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Enthalpy of neutralisation of strong monobasic acid with strong monoacidic base is always −57 kJ mol^{−1}. Reason (R): Enthalpy of neutralisation is the amount of heat liberated when one mole of H^{+} ions furnished by acid combine with one mole of ^{−}OH ions furnished by base to form one mole of water. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
sol: Strong acid + strong base are fully ionised, so the only reaction is H^{+} + OH^{−} → H_{2}O, about −57 kJ every time — R explains A.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

pyq.q: For the reaction at 298 K, 2A + B → C. ΔH = 400 kJ mol^{−1} and ΔS = 0.2 kJ mol^{−1} K^{−1}. The reaction will become spontaneous above ____ K.
When ΔH_{vap} = 30 kJ/mol and ΔS_{vap} = 75 J mol^{−1} K^{−1}, then the temperature of vapour, at one atmosphere is ____ K.
sol: At the boiling point ΔG = 0: T = \f{30 000}{75} = 400 K.

pyq.q: Ice at −5 °C is heated to become vapor with temperature of 110 °C at atmospheric pressure. The entropy change associated with this process can be obtained from
sol: Heating: ΔS = ∫\f{C_{p}}{T}dT for each phase (ice, water, steam). Phase change: ΔS = \f{ΔH}{T} at that temperature.
Only (2) divides every heating step by T; (1) and (4) give enthalpy, not entropy.

pyq.q: The standard enthalpy and standard entropy of decomposition of N_{2}O_{4} to NO_{2} are 55.0 kJ mol^{−1} and 175.0 J/K/mol respectively. The standard free energy change for this reaction at 25 °C in J mol^{−1} is ____. (Nearest integer)

The effect of temperature on spontaneity of reactions are represented as : (A) ΔH +, ΔS −, any T, Non spontaneous; (B) ΔH +, ΔS +, low T, spontaneous; (C) ΔH −, ΔS −, low T, Non spontaneous; (D) ΔH −, ΔS +, any T, spontaneous. The incorrect combinations are:
sol: (B) +, +: spontaneous only at HIGH T ✗. (C) −, −: spontaneous at LOW T ✗. (A) and (D) are right.

pyq.q: Let us consider an endothermic reaction which is non-spontaneous at the freezing point of water. However, the reaction is spontaneous at boiling point of water. Choose the correct option.
sol: Endothermic → ΔH > 0. Spontaneous only at higher T means −TΔS must win as T rises → ΔS > 0.

pyq.q: Standard entropies of X_{2}, Y_{2} and XY_{5} are 70, 50 and 110 J K^{−1} mol^{−1} respectively. The temperature in Kelvin at which the reaction \f{1}{2}X_{2} + \f{5}{2}Y_{2} ⇌ XY_{5}, ΔH° = −35 kJ mol^{−1} will be at equilibrium is ____ (Nearest integer)
Which of the following is not correct ?
o: ΔG is negative for a spontaneous reaction
ΔG is positive for a spontaneous reaction
ΔG is zero for a reversible reaction
ΔG is positive for a non-spontaneous reaction

words: Measure of energy spreading or disorder
Device that measures heat of a reaction
Property that does not depend on amount
Happens on its own without outside help
Regular 3D arrangement of ions in a crystal
